name: Question 4
problem:
Consider the linear transformation
$T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x+4y \\ y+z \\ x-4z\end{aligned}]$ and the vectors 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$ Which of the given vectors belong to $\text{Ker}(T)?$
worked_solution:
A vector $u$ belongs to the kernel of a linear transformation $T$ if $T(u)=0.$ 

Therefore, we need to compute $T({v}_{i})$ for each ${v}_{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T({v}_{1}) & =T([\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T({v}_{2}) & =T([\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T({v}_{3}) & =T([\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Since $T({v}_{1})=T({v}_{2})=T({v}_{3})=0,$ we conclude that the vectors that belong to the kernel of $T$ are ${v}_{1},$ ${v}_{2},$ and ${v}_{3}.$

Question 4
?

Consider the linear transformation T:[xyz]⟶[x+4yy+zx−4z] and the vectors v1=[4−11],v2=[−41−1],v3=[000]. Which of the given vectors belong to Ker(T)?

a
v2 and v3 only
b
v1 only
c
v1 and v3 only
d
v1, v2, and v3
e
v1 and v2, only
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

A vector u belongs to the kernel of a linear transformation T if T(u)=0.

Therefore, we need to compute T(vi) for each vi: T(v1)=T([4−11])=[000]T(v2)=T([−41−1])=[000]T(v3)=T([000])=[000]

Since T(v1)=T(v2)=T(v3)=0, we conclude that the vectors that belong to the kernel of T are v1, v2, and v3.
